In this repo (Show Command Center, pnpm monorepo), examine the full Drizzle ORM schema and task-related backend/frontend code to prepare for planning a Todoist two-way sync integration.

Please report:
1. Full contents (or relevant excerpts) of the Drizzle schema file(s) in lib/db/ — specifically the `shows`, `tasks`, `eblasts`, `office_tasks`, and `links` table definitions. Include all columns, types, defaults, and any existing external-id/sync-related columns.
2. The backend route handlers for tasks (artifacts/api-server/src/routes/ — the shows/:showId/tasks routes, office-tasks routes, and eblasts routes). How is task completion (`completed`/`completedAt`) currently set — PATCH endpoint? What fields can be updated?
3. Any existing webhook or external-API-call infrastructure in the api-server (look for outbound HTTP clients, webhook route handlers, or scheduled jobs/cron).
4. The frontend components that toggle task completion (task-list.tsx, eblast-list.tsx, office-tasks page) — how do they call the API on checkbox toggle?
5. The OpenAPI spec (lib/api-spec/openapi.yaml) — list the endpoints related to tasks/office-tasks/eblasts and their schemas.
6. Any existing preset/category logic for tasks (task-list.tsx presets) — just a brief summary of structure, not full enumeration.

Report file paths and relevant code snippets/line numbers.

- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. ## 3. Existing outbound-HTTP / webhook / sync infrastructure

There is **no webhook receiver and no cron/scheduled job** anywhere in `artifacts/api-server/src` (grep for cron/schedule/webhook/setInterval returned nothing). All sync is **manually triggered, one-way (app → provider)**, via these two symmetric modules:

- `/home/runner/workspace/artifacts/api-server/src/lib/todoist-client.ts` — uses `@replit/connectors-sdk`'s `ReplitConnectors().proxy("todoist", path, ...)` to call the Todoist REST API (v1) through Replit's managed OAuth connector (no manual token handling). Exposes:
  - `todoistRequest(method, path, body)` — generic proxy call with 429 retry/backoff (up to 5 retries, exponential + jitter). Returns `null` on 404 (used as a "deleted upstream" signal).
  - `todoistListProjects()` — `GET /api/v1/projects`.
  - `makeTodoistTask(content, description, dueDate, projectId?)` — builds request body; hardcodes `due_string: "${dueDate} 09:00"`.

- `/home/runner/workspace/artifacts/api-server/src/lib/google-calendar-client.ts` — identical pattern for Google Calendar via the `"google-calendar"` connector.

- `/home/runner/workspace/artifacts/api-server/src/routes/todoist.ts` (mounted at `/export/todoist`):
  - `GET /projects` → lists Todoist projects for a picker UI.
  - `POST /sync?showId=&taskProjectId=&eblastProjectId=` → pulls all tasks/eblasts (optionally scoped to one show), pushes each to Todoist with `CONCURRENCY=5` batching: creates if no `todoistTaskId`, else updates via `POST /api/v1/tasks/:id` (falls back to create if that 404s, meaning it was deleted on the Todoist side — it does NOT currently detect and pull down remote edits, just treats 404 as "recreate"). Also calls `setTodoistCompletion()` which does `POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/close` or `/reopen` to mirror local `completed`/`sent` state to Todoist. Tasks/eblasts with no `dueDate` get deleted from Todoist (Todoist has no concept of due-date-less item in this app's model). Finally drains `todoist_orphans` (deletes stray remote tasks).
  - **This is one-way push only** — nothing reads Todoist state back into the local DB, so there is no existing "pull" or webhook path; that's the main gap for true two-way sync.

- `/home/runner/workspace/artifacts/api-server/src/routes/google-calendar.ts` (mounted at `/export/google-calendar`) — same architecture for GCal, useful as a second reference implementation of the create/update/orphan-drain pattern.

- `office_tasks` are **not included in either sync route** — only `tasksTable`/`eblastsTable` are synced today.
